title: REST APIs and JSON
subtitle: An API is a contract between programs: what to ask, in what shape, and what comes back.

sections.title: REST principles
sections.body: REST models an API as resources with URLs (/books, /books/7) and uses HTTP methods as verbs: GET read, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH change, DELETE remove. Stateless requests; standard status codes (201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found). Nouns in URLs, not verbs: DELETE /books/7, not /deleteBook.

questions.prompt: Which is RESTful for deleting book 7?

responses.title: A tempting idea.
responses.body: Verb in the URL, unsafe GET.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Verb is the method; noun is the URL.

sections.title: JSON
sections.body: JSON is text for objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null: {"id": 7, "title": "SICP", "tags": ["cs"]}. JSON.stringify / JSON.parse convert. Keys are quoted with double quotes; no trailing commas, no comments.

sections.title: A CRUD conversation
sections.body: Creating returns 201 and the new resource; reading returns 200; updating returns 200 or 204; deleting 204; a missing id 404.

questions.prompt: A successful POST that creates a resource returns…

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: With the new resource or its URL.

figures.caption: Figure 4.3.1 — CRUD over HTTP
figures.note: The same URL changes meaning with the method.

sections.title: Idempotence and safety
sections.body: Safe methods (GET) change nothing. Idempotent methods (GET, PUT, DELETE) give the same final state if repeated; POST is not — retrying it may create two orders. Use an idempotency key for payments.

worked.why: Final state is the same both times — it is idempotent.

sections.title: Authentication for APIs
sections.body: Clients send a credential with each request: an API key, or a bearer token in Authorization: Bearer …. OAuth 2.0 lets a user grant an app limited access without sharing a password; JWTs are signed, self-describing tokens (header.payload.signature) the server can verify without a lookup.

choices.text: Granting limited access without sharing the password.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: The user logs in only at the auth server.

figures.caption: Figure 4.5.1 — OAuth code flow
figures.note: The app never sees the password.

sections.title: Good API design
sections.body: Version the API (/v1/); paginate lists (?page=2&limit=20); return consistent error bodies; rate-limit; document with OpenAPI. Status 429 tells a client to slow down.

problems.prompt: 2,345 records at 50 per page. How many pages?
